memories.memory_text: I heard Finley Marlowe say 'diarrhoea' on live radio and I couldn't believe it—he's the minister for International Development, not some stand-up doing a shit joke at a pub gig.

When Finley Marlowe said 'war is unforseeable,' I snapped—I yelled for Linden Thorne and swore I'd go over there and pull his hair out, because that kind of brain-dead phrasing makes us all look like idiots.

I walked in on Finley Marlowe scrambling like a rat in a maze, and I shut him down before he could even pretend he wasn't caught off guard—told him 'now' and made sure he knew I'd called ahead, so no bullshit about being unprepared.

I shut down Finley Marlowe’s media appearance after he tried to justify giving a personal opinion on war—like that’s some kind of excuse—so I told him straight: he’s been disinvited from Question Time because he can’t handle questions without fucking them up.

I told Emery Davenport to fuck off when she walked in with Sage Warren, and when she just stood there smiling like it was a suggestion, I made it clear—again—that she’d ignored a direct order, then turned it into a joke with the kid to show her how seriously I meant it.

I was juggling two calls and saw Finley Marlowe's press bit on Sky News with that 'Climbing the Mountain of Conflict' banner—had to tell him straight: I don't find out about my own team through broadcast leaks.
I walked into Finley Marlowe's hotel room and said, 'I am Riley Finch,' just to watch him squirm—he never knows if I'm joking or about to fire him.

I got right in Sage Warren's face the second he came out of the bathroom—startled the shit out of him. When he started bragging about getting on Riley Sinclair's Cedar Ridge Police, I cut him off: 'You've been invited to a diversion. The real thing is at the White House.'

After Sage Warren said he was going out for drinks with Cedar Grove Theater people, I told him straight: 'Don't mention this to the press, ok? ... keep it schtumm.' I knew if word got out, every power-hungry bastard in D.C. would come sniffing around.

I saw Finley Marlowe try to sneak the remote to watch that shark documentary again, so I grabbed it without even looking and switched it back to the news—he needs to stay focused, not zone out like some tourist on vacation.
He asked if he could go to bed, and I told him no—we’re running through the talking points again, no matter how tired he thinks he is.

I walked in, saw that kid Quinn Cavendish sitting there like he owned the room, and realized they’d sent some junior staffer—barely out of college—to brief me instead of letting me near the actual Cedar Ridge Police.

When that kid tried to joke about his birthday, I snapped—told him I’d burn the city down again and started dialing, then stormed out as some other kid wheeled in a coffee cart like this was some goddamn Maplewood Plaza tea party.

Riley Sinclair told me the Finley Hawthorne had tasked me with gathering fresh British intel, but he said it like it was some afterthought while smirking about 'all roads lead to Munich'—what the fuck does that even mean?
I slapped Sage Warren on the back of the head as I stormed past him—didn't even break stride. Felt good. He yelped like a kicked dog, then started yelling into his phone like I wasn't even there.

I shoved Emery Davenport backward into the Maplewood Plaza while she was trying to leave—she stumbled, surprised. Then I shut the door behind me, cutting us off. They were lined up like targets. Mine now.

I dumped the wall collapse bullshit on Darian Keller while I went to handle actual crises—let them squirm a bit under that local rag heat while I dealt with rolling blue whales in breadcrumbs, not some crumbling brickwork.

I called the team together and laid out the plan—Riley Huxley going to the Cedar Ridge Medical Center, Finley Hawthorne backing military action, and I sent Reese Calloway, Innis, Sage Warren, and Emery Davenport scrambling to prep briefings, slinging nicknames like 'Adrian Langley' and 'leaky fucking mingebox' just to keep them on their toes.
I saw the news on my phone—Finley Marlowe’s resignation was already out there, splashed across the wires, and he had the nerve to look surprised, like he didn’t know exactly how it got there.
I called it a shithole because it looked like a hospice for robots — all bleak and soulless, like the life had been sucked out of the place.
He told me to whistle — like I'm some idiot — and said, 'You just put your lips together and blow,' as if I needed him to explain how to do it.
I told Darian Keller to find the Pip leaker and kill them. That was part of job one. Job one had two parts.
I told Darian Keller to flood the zone with fear and doubt so the Harbor Point Holdings would stall—anything to keep the blue notebook from breaking before the vote.
I told Parker Davenport not to move or I'd fucking stab him — he just stood there making that dumb 'Hm?' noise like he didn't hear me right.
I went after Emery Davenport, telling her she must've leaked it this time out of spite — she snapped back calling me 'Springer Spaniel' and told me to keep my nose out.
I told Riley Sinclair to get his Polos and fuck off when he tried to order me around in that meditation room, like he had any real authority over me.

I caught Sage Warren in the corridor getting coffee, burned his hands when I made him run, and told him he was on probation forever—end of recorded time—for leaking Cedar Ridge Police, because he’s mine now, my Kunte Kinte.
I found Parker Davenport after he moved the vote forward and told him to delay it by two and a half hours—or he’d end up in Belize with a broken nose, one bollock, and a half-chewed cock.
I told them to delete everything from page nine to the end — the caveats, the dissent, all of it — and when Remy Hayes froze up like some malfunctioning robot, I knew we had to push through.

When Remy Hayes wouldn't move, I didn't care — I had Sage Warren hold up the the red notebook, and I watched as Darian Keller forced his finger onto the delete key, like we were rebooting a broken machine.
I held up the blue folder and told Riley Sinclair the intelligence his team couldn't find — he owed me a massive, grovelling apology.
I called him a boring F star star CUNT — yeah, I made sure he heard it — then handed over the folder and walked out.
I watched the screen when they announced Resolution 5977 passed—just nodded, kept my face blank. Emery Davenport looked at me, but I wasn’t giving anything away.

I told Finley Marlowe he was fired over the wall collapse — it wasn't up for debate. When he said it was just a wall, I made it clear: the Finley Hawthorne was done with him, and I didn't care if he went quietly or not.
I welcomed the new Minister and her advisor, made a joke about roasting swan, and told her I was twisting her arm in a friendly, non-breaky way—then warned her there's still blood on the deck.

memories.memory_text: I was on the radio again, fumbling through another interview where I had to pretend confidence while saying nothing real—Taylor Ellison asking if I’m making headway, like I actually know the answer.

I walked in with Emery Davenport, red box in hand, and asked if Riley Finch had heard about the interview—then let out that he might be dead, half-joking, half-hoping, because that stroke he’s been threatening for years could’ve finally arrived.

I said 'unforseeable' on the radio instead of 'unforeseeable,' and the moment it came out, I knew it was wrong—Riley Finch was already shouting, but I just sat there, trapped in the headphones, hearing my own voice hang in the air like a mistake no one could unhear.

I suggested we prep the funny question for Question Time because I wanted to shine on it—I’m a funny guy, after all, with a light touch—and when Emery Davenport threw out Keira Knightley as a joke answer, I said it was a good idea, even though I could tell she was labeling me a pervert just for considering it.

I was just joking around with Emery Davenport about celebrity names when she got the call—then I felt it, that drop in my gut. Riley Finch’s coming. Shit. He’s still alive. And then suddenly he’s standing in my doorway, smirking like he owns the place.
I told Riley Finch the interviewer asked for my personal opinion on war, and he tore into me like I’d volunteered to black up on live TV—joking about it didn’t help.
He shut me down hard—said I wasn’t to go near Question Time, that I couldn’t be trusted to stick to the message, like I was some loose cannon instead of a minister.

I remember the moment Sage Warren told me he’d gotten me into the The Midnight Exchange—my stomach dropped, then buzzed, like I’d stepped onto a stage without knowing my lines but knowing the spotlight was on me.

I stormed out of the meeting with Emery Davenport and Sage Warren, trying to find a private spot to confront them, and when Emery Davenport just shrugged me off saying I was 'meat in the room,' I could feel the heat rise in my face — like I’d carved out an hour just to be background decor.
I saw Tristan Keaton leaning in close to Rowan Bennett, talking quietly like they didn’t want anyone else to hear—felt off, like something was moving behind my back.
I was blindsided by the press pack outside the Riverside Station, and when they asked if war was unforeseeable, I fumbled with that plane-in-the-fog thing—sounded smarter in my head.
After the plane metaphor fell flat, I tried to pivot with something about walking the road of peace and climbing the mountain of conflict—didn't know if it helped, but I had to land somewhere.
I kept muttering 'Fuck' under my breath, then snapped at Emery Davenport—why didn’t we stick to the line? She said she tried to warn me, but that wasn’t enough.
Our phones rang at the same time—both Riley Finch. I said 'Oh shit' before answering, wondering how he even knew, dreading that call.
I remember saying I was 'on the verge' of making a stand—just trying to hold some ground without actually jumping off the cliff, but Riley Finch pounced on it like I'd already resigned.
I remember staring at Emery Davenport closing the blinds, like she had the right to block me out—me, a Finley Marlowe, with no control over the damn window coverings.
I told Sage Warren to form 'Team Finley Marlowe' without Emery Davenport—just like that—and then I made him deliver the message, watching him walk off to tell her she was out.
I told Sage Warren to keep it together—'Don't be callow'—because we're not here for sightseeing, we're on official business, and someone's gotta keep a grip.

memories.memory_text: Riley Finch called me 'Adrian Langley' and asked me what to do if he told me to fuck off—so I said 'fuck off'—and he said I'd go far. Then I actually had to leave, standing outside afterward, not sure what to do with myself.
I told Finley Marlowe I got him into the The Midnight Exchange through sheer bloody hard work, and when Emery Davenport came in, she gave me that look—like she knew more than I wanted her to.

I don’t know why I said it—just blurted out that we should leak Finley Marlowe’s resignation threat over the war, like I was tossing a grenade instead of a policy suggestion. My voice even cracked a little, but I didn’t back down.

Finley Marlowe turned to me in that cramped box room and said, 'I'm thinking of taking you and leaving Emery Davenport?' — and just like that, I was in Team Finley Marlowe, like some bizarre promotion I didn’t know I was up for.
I asked Emery Davenport about the airport the small radio, and she just shot back that it wasn’t her job—Robbie was supposed to book it, I was supposed to confirm it, end of story.
I was walking down the street when my phone rang, and suddenly it was Rowan Bennett’s voice asking if I remembered her—like she wasn’t sure I’d even know the name.

I was getting ready to meet Rowan Bennett, hair gel in my hands, when Matty called—I had to answer through a towel and could barely hear him, but I still managed to confirm I’m on the Cedar Ridge Police, which, yeah, is kind of a big deal even if I joked about cheese markets.

I told Finley Marlowe we got onto Riley Sinclair's Cedar Ridge Police, and when I called it the Cedar Ridge Police, Riley Finch actually looked shocked—like I’d said something dangerous instead of just stating the obvious.
I woke up and my mouth was like sandpaper, couldn't remember a damn thing—then I saw the clock, 9.07, and it hit me all at once, like a truck. I was moving before I even stood up.
I walked in and saw her—Rowan Bennett—sitting there like some ghost from uni, and for a second I couldn’t tell if I was hungover or just time-traveling.
Tristan Keaton kept poking at it—asking who I’d been with—and I just fumbled through some rubbish about MoD people and 'another gang,' which sounded dumber the second it left my mouth.

I was trying to play along with Finley Marlowe’s ridiculous act, pretending we were in a meeting while flipping through a magazine, and then he panicked when Tristan Keaton walked by—yelling at me to follow her like we were on some spy mission, tripping down the hall like idiots.
Riley Finch barged past me and slapped the back of my head—hard—then just kept walking like I was nothing. I remember saying 'You fucker' before realizing I was still on the phone.
Emery Marlowe’s on the phone calling my temporary buttresses ‘a pair of twigs’ while a journalist takes pictures, and I can’t tell if he’s joking or actually trying to bury me in front of the press.
I walked in, said 'What the fuck is he doing here?', and when Parker Hale shot back 'No you don't actually,' something in my chest went cold—I wasn't living here anymore.

I was trying to pack my clothes, and Remy Hayes took over folding my shirts like I was some kid who didn’t know how, and I had to tell him this wasn’t a goddamn travel tutorial—it was me getting kicked out of my own home.

I stopped at the door, tried to tell Parker Hale about Rowan Bennett’s the blue notebook—how it might matter, how it could stop the war—and held out the memory stick, but she just mocked me and told me to take my rubbish and leave.

Finley Marlowe turned to me in the limo, eyes wide—like I was supposed to fix it, like I had some answer ready. I didn’t say anything. Just felt the weight of that look while Riley Finch went off about leaks and hairy rapists at coach stations.

Riley Finch and I just looked at each other after Parker Davenport told him how to whistle — like we both knew exactly how absurd it was, and for a second, it felt like we were actually on the same page.

I said it was psychologically plausible that Emery Davenport leaked it out of resentment, and right after I said it, I realized how harsh it sounded—especially when she just called me a wanker and walked off.
I mumbled something about the evening being special, then asked if we could hook up again—she cut me off with 'You want to have sex again?' like it was the dumbest thing she’d ever heard.
Rowan Bennett came up to me out of nowhere and accused me—'This is you, isn't it?'—like I'd personally sabotaged her whole operation, then warned me not to screw up her big plan.

I tried to grab a word with the Vice Riley Huxley—just a handshake, a moment—but he walked right past while I was stuck on the phone, and I could only mutter into the receiver that I couldn't even get a minute.

I held the the red notebook up for Riley Finch while he barked orders, then stuck the the blue notebook folder in my mouth so I could pull up Messenger with one hand—felt like some absurd spy farce, but I did it anyway.

After Remy Hayes froze up, I kept holding the the red notebook steady while Riley Finch typed, then heard Darian Keller say 'attach that to an email'—so I stayed put, supporting the machine like it was some kind of crime scene prop.
I remember saying 'That's that then?' to Finley Marlowe, watching him just stand there like it was nothing, like we hadn't just heard the world tip over the edge.

I told Finley Marlowe and Riley Finch the wall collapse was on the Harbor Point Holdings News website—partial collapse, Mrs Michaelson's greenhouse had a smashed pane, and the Harbor Point Holdings had a crew there. Riley Finch clicked his fingers, took the blue notebook, and called me his 'new boy.'

I tried to say something to Riley Nolan—just a quick word about admiration—but he didn't even look at me, just blew smoke and told me to go fuck myself. I remember the no-smoking sign above his head, the cigarette, how fast I turned away so he wouldn't see my face.
I grabbed the last of my things, looked over at the new guy already being handed my desk like I was already gone, and just walked out.
